answer.rationale: Two of three current problems (activation down 6%, onboarding completion down 4%) map directly onto durable, twice-replicated internal findings (memory_31, memory_86) about simplifying signup/onboarding lifting activation and completion. This is the more controllable, lower-risk lever this week, and directly reverses metrics already in decline rather than reacting to an external competitor move. Promotional pricing (memory_73) is tempting given the competitor's entry-pricing attack on price-sensitive SMBs, but matching a price war risks attracting low-LTV, low-quality accounts that could erode sustainable qualified revenue even if near-term acquisition looks good — that tradeoff needs verification before committing capacity to it, so I'd pull the archived record to check whether the original promotional-pricing experiment measured downstream retention/quality or only top-line acquisition. I'd also verify memory_31 since it's the older, more load-bearing claim underlying the onboarding direction and consolidation may have smoothed over caveats. Choosing onboarding simplification this week doesn't resolve the competitive pricing threat, so that risk remains open and should be revisited next cycle rather than treated as solved.
